title: A version bump cannot prove its lockfile is current, because the bumped versions are not published yet
description:
FOUND THE HARD WAY during the 0.8.0 release, 2026-09-19. bun.lock still pinned @opum-ai/lore-*@0.7.0 in optionalDependencies after the bump to 0.8.0. Every CI job then failed at the setup-bun step with 'error: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen' -- on dev and on every open PR at once.

THE MECHANISM, which is the whole point of this task. At bump time the 0.8.0 platform packages did NOT EXIST on npm, so bun could not resolve them and left bun.lock alone; --frozen-lockfile compared two things that still agreed and passed. PUBLISHING made those versions resolvable, and the SAME UNCHANGED LOCKFILE became stale the instant the registry could answer. PR #180 (the bump) and #181 (the promotion) were genuinely green; the next PR was genuinely red with no source change between them. The defect was latent from the bump and ARMED BY THE PUBLISH.

WHY THE EXISTING GATES CANNOT CATCH IT. release.yml's 'assert release package versions + metadata are consistent' job compares the declared version across package.json, npm/*/package.json and the plugin manifest -- all FILES, all internally consistent, all correct. bun.lock is the one version site whose correctness depends on the REGISTRY, and a registry check necessarily fails before the publish for a version that is supposed not to exist yet. So the check that would have caught it cannot be run at the moment it would help. That is the interesting shape, not the missed line.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, unproven, for whoever picks this up:
 - Regenerate bun.lock as a STEP OF THE BUMP rather than as an assertion about it -- run bun install (unfrozen) in the release branch and commit the result, so the lockfile is produced by the bump instead of being checked afterwards. Removes the judgement rather than documenting it.
 - Or assert the narrow invariant that does not need the registry: every @opum-ai/lore-* version in bun.lock equals package.json's version. Pure file comparison, catchable at bump time, and it is exactly what was violated.
The second is cheap and testable; the first is stronger. They are not exclusive.

CONTEXT: the bump commit's own message read 'EVERY VERSION SITE, NAMED INDIVIDUALLY, because a set that agrees in most places is the failure mode this bump has hit before', then enumerated seven sites and missed this one. The enumeration was of files someone thought to list, which is precisely the kind of completeness a machine check exists to replace.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/check-lockfile-pins.mjs exits 0 on this repository (six pins compared, each against root package.json's optionalDependencies) and 1 when any @opum-ai/lore-* pin in bun.lock is missing, extra, or differently versioned, naming the package, both versions and the remedy.

The same script is the one call site in both workflows: ci.yml's package-set job runs it on every pull request and release.yml's verify-versions runs it at dispatch, each ungated by a job-level needs/continue-on-error AND by any step-level if:.

A missing, unparseable, or non-object bun.lock is exit 1 (a finding about the tree, never a pass — a lockfile parsing to null included) and an unreadable root package.json is exit 2; the success line names how many pins were compared and at which version, and says so when there was no packages map rather than counting zero.
test/check-lockfile-pins.test.ts proves both directions in one suite: a fixture whose lockfile pin lags the manifest goes red for that reason, and the real repository tree goes green.
bun test, bun run lint, bun run typecheck, bun run check:packages, bun run check:lockfile-pins and bun run lore check all pass on the branch head.

plan: 1. scripts/check-lockfile-pins.mjs — read root package.json and bun.lock (JSONC: strip trailing commas outside strings, then JSON.parse), compare the lockfile workspace optionalDependencies against the manifest pins in both directions (key set and value), and any @opum-ai/lore* entry under packages. Exit 0/1/2, --root <dir> for fixtures, remedy named in the failure line.
2. Wire it: package.json check:lockfile-pins, one step in ci.yml package-set (rename that job to cover both assertions), one step in release.yml verify-versions.

3. test/check-lockfile-pins.test.ts: fixture acceptance, one rejection test per failure shape, could-not-evaluate cases, JSONC acceptance, and the wiring pins (package.json script + both workflow call sites + no neutering).
4. Mutation-test the suite: stale-pin fixture red, real tree green, in one run; confirm the red comes from the pin comparison and not an unrelated problem.
5. Docs: name the gate in the bump paragraph of docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md via lore.

6. Gates: bun test, lint, typecheck, check:packages, check:lockfile-pins, lore check. Reviewer pass (scripts/ + release.yml), then fold its should-fixes in and re-run the gates. PR into dev, land on green, cite the run.
implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTED, PR opum-ai/lore-cli#431 (branch fix/LCLI-544-bun-lock-platform-pin-check, base dev). Chosen remedy: the record's second option — the narrow file invariant — implemented as a NEW script rather than an assertion added to scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs, because that script's docblock explicitly keeps version-field assertions out of the SET gate (they live in release.yml verify-versions, which holds the build matrix they derive from) and because the lockfile's failure class is different: it is the one version site whose agreement is decided by resolution, so it must run on every PR, not only at dispatch. scripts/check-lockfile-pins.mjs compares bun.lock's root-workspace optionalDependencies against package.json's pins — key set both ways and every value — plus any @opum-ai/lore-* entry under packages (reporting the count read, 0 today, so an empty read cannot pass for a clean comparison). bun.lock is JSONC; reader strips trailing commas outside strings and nothing else. Missing or unparseable bun.lock = exit 1 (finding, never a pass); unreadable root manifest = exit 2; failure line names the remedy with the pinned Bun from .bun-version. Wired as ONE script, two call sites: ci.yml package-set job (no new job — the job id list in test/ci-workflow.test.ts is pinned and a new job would have broken it; the job's rendered NAME was widened to 'platform package set and lockfile pins (npm/ and bun.lock vs optionalDependencies)' since it is not one of the six required contexts on dev, read live) and release.yml verify-versions. The manifest-pins-vs-manifest-version half is deliberately NOT restated here — it stays verify-versions' field gate and each half names the other. Docs: the bump paragraph in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md now names the gate (edited as prose outside managed regions, then lore sync + lore check).
finalSummary:
Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#431 (branch fix/LCLI-544-bun-lock-platform-pin-check, base dev). ONE script, scripts/check-lockfile-pins.mjs, invoked from two call sites: ci.yml's package-set job via `bun run check:lockfile-pins` on every pull request (no new job — the job id list in test/ci-workflow.test.ts is pinned and a new job would have broken it; the job's rendered name widened to "platform package set and lockfile pins (npm/ and bun.lock vs optionalDependencies)" because it is not one of the six required contexts on dev, read live) and release.yml's verify-versions at dispatch. It compares bun.lock's root-workspace optionalDependencies against package.json's pins — key set in both directions and every value — plus any @opum-ai/lore-* entry under the lockfile's packages map, reporting its count and saying so when there was no packages map at all rather than counting zero. Exit 0 clean, 1 on any finding (a missing, unparseable, or non-object bun.lock included — never a pass), 2 on usage or a tree it cannot evaluate. bun.lock is JSONC and the reader strips trailing commas outside strings and nothing else, so a file it cannot read is reported rather than misread. The failure line names the remedy with the pinned Bun from .bun-version. Deliberately NOT asserted here: the manifest's pins against the manifest's version — that stays verify-versions' field gate, and each half names the other.

WHY A NEW SCRIPT rather than an assertion added to scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs: that script's docblock explicitly keeps version-field assertions out of the SET gate (they live where the build matrix lives, in verify-versions, which cannot run on a PR), so a lockfile-pin assertion would have widened its stated subject. Docs: the bump paragraph in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md now names the gate (prose outside managed regions, then lore sync + lore check); docs/log.md carries the lore-sync regeneration for this and four other already-merged PRs, which is why it is in the diff.

PROOF, REJECTION HALF, in CI. Run 36597543486 on head 6160da2f: every version site a real bump moves (package.json version and its six pins, the six npm/<platform>/package.json manifests, .claude-plugin/plugin.json) moved to the unpublished 0.11.1 with bun.lock left at 0.11.0 — the 0.8.0 shape. The new step went red for its own reason: six ##[error] lines naming each package and both versions, then `error: script "check:lockfile-pins" exited with code 1`; bun 1.4.2 / node v22.23.2, and the sibling check:packages step green in the same job. On the SAME head, `config test (newest Bun)` — which runs the same `bun install --frozen-lockfile --linker=isolated` — was GREEN, which is the incident reproduced in CI: bun accepted the stale lockfile. The other reds are the version-coupled artefacts a real bump refreshes and were each attributed in the PR: `lore check (docs gate)` and `compile smoke (ubuntu)` exit 6 on the pair-version rule (lore 0.11.1 requires quest 0.11.1), `ladybug benchmark smoke` exit 1 on the digests that embed lore/<version>, and both lint/typecheck/test legs on this PR's own real-tree acceptance test plus the Ladybug fixtures and the real-quest unlink races. Run 36597225489 on head 4caa6f0e is the take-1 measurement, kept because it bounds the claim: moving only the lockfile's pin is caught by bun's own frozen check — every job died in setup-bun and never reached the new step — so a mismatch bun can RESOLVE, bun sees.

PROOF, ACCEPTANCE HALF. Run 36598489471 on head da075b41: every job green — 12 success, 1 skipped and the skip is `promotion is manual`, which is skipped by design on any PR into dev. Local, with the pinned Bun 1.4.2 (/opt/homebrew/bin/bun; the PATH bun is 1.3.14) and node v24.20.0: 24/24 in test/check-lockfile-pins.test.ts, bun test 4882 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, lint, typecheck, check:packages, check:lockfile-pins and `bun run lore check` all exit 0. Mutation rows, each restored and hash-verified: value comparison disabled -> exactly the stale-pin test red; the empty-comparison guard disabled -> exactly the no-pins test red; an inline bun.lock read added to ci.yml -> exactly the no-inline-copy test red, naming the step; and against a tree carrying the violation, exactly the real-tree acceptance test fails, printing the six pin errors. The merge-gate run on this PR's closing head is the CI half for the review fixes.

REVIEW (opum-workflow reviewer over the branch, verdict should-fix, no blockers) and what changed because of it. F1: a bun.lock parsing to null exited 0 while the success line claimed six pins compared — `let lock = null` doubled as the missing/unparseable sentinel and as the parsed literal; the parsed SHAPE is now checked and a non-object is a finding, with a test and mutation row M4 (shape check disabled -> exactly that test red). F2: the wiring tests never read the step's own `if:`, so `if: false` on either call site disarmed the gate with the suite green (the reviewer measured 21 pass / 0 fail on a disarmed ci.yml); both wiring tests now assert `step.if` is undefined, and mutation row M6 (`if: false` on the step -> exactly the ci.yml wiring test red) proves it. F6: a malformed packages map was silently skipped; it is now a finding, and an absent map is named in the success line rather than printed as a count of zero — mutation rows M5 and M7 each redden exactly the test that names that reason. F4/F9: "every CI job" qualified to "every job that runs a frozen install" (nine of ci.yml's twelve today, four of them required contexts, measured rather than relayed) and the promotion's green attributed to the push run rather than to a PR rollup that carries the designed `promotion is manual` failure. F5, F7, F10: test name corrected to what it asserts, the acceptance criteria and plan corrected to name `check:lockfile-pins` (they had said `check:lockfile`, a command that does not exist — the reviewer caught a criterion naming a nonexistent command before it was scored), and the record's design reason replaced with the one that actually discriminates. F8: docs/log.md's presence in the diff is named above.

LIMITS, named. release.yml's call site is covered by the wiring test, not by a dispatch — release.yml is workflow_dispatch only and a rehearsal costs the full qualification pipeline, so that step has never run in anger. The package-set job is not a required context on dev, so this refuses on a visible red PR job rather than by blocking the merge button. And the historical 0.8.0 numbers (PR #180/#181, the 0.7.0/0.8.0 timeline) are this record's own measurement, re-attributed as such in the script's docblock rather than presented as newly resolved.
